claim: Zionism is racism: the United Nations said so.

heard.quote: determines that Zionism is a form of racism and racial discrimination
the unholy alliance between South African racism and Zionism

answer: On 10 November 1975 the UN General Assembly voted 72 to 35, with 32 abstentions, that Zionism is a form of racism. The UN roll call lists the Soviet bloc, China, Arab and Muslim states, India, and also Brazil, Mexico, Portugal and Malta voting yes; the United States, Israel and most Western European states voted no. Israel's ambassador Chaim Herzog and US ambassador Daniel Patrick Moynihan denounced it that day. On 16 December 1991 the Assembly revoked it, 111 to 25, with 13 abstentions, as the Soviet bloc collapsed. Today, by UN Watch's count, the Assembly passed 173 resolutions on Israel against 80 on all other countries together from 2015 to 2024, and the Human Rights Council keeps a standing agenda item on Israel; the UN keeps no official count, and a fact check says such counts do not by themselves prove bias.

facts.text: The roll call recorded in the UN's text of Resolution 3379 shows who voted how. In favour (72): the Soviet Union, the Ukrainian and Byelorussian republics, Poland, Hungary, Czechoslovakia, Bulgaria, East Germany, Albania, Mongolia, Cuba and Yugoslavia; China; the Arab states that voted, among them Egypt, Algeria, Iraq, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Libya, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Syria, Tunisia, Morocco and Yemen; Iran, Pakistan, Indonesia, Turkey, India and Sri Lanka; and Brazil, Mexico, Portugal, Malta and Cyprus. Against (35): the United States, Israel, the United Kingdom, France, West Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Belgium, Austria, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, the five Nordic states, Ireland and Luxembourg, and several Latin American and African states (among them Haiti, Honduras, Nicaragua, Panama, Costa Rica, El Salvador, Uruguay, Ivory Coast, Liberia and Malawi). Abstaining (32): among them Greece, Japan, Argentina, Chile, Colombia, Venezuela, Peru, Philippines, Thailand, Singapore, Kenya and Ethiopia.

contested.text: Whether the numbers show bias. The Scripps fact check says the count documents the volume of attention on Israel but 'against Israel' is UN Watch's label, not a UN classification, and the count does not by itself prove the reason for the disparity or a systemic bias; the General Assembly has also adopted resolutions on Palestinian rights.

contested.text: Why Israel gets so many resolutions. could_not_verify: The list of sponsors of the 1975 text. The Third Committee records and the UN Digital Library documents that list co-sponsors could not be read; I could confirm only that Somalia introduced the resolution (EBSCO) and that it was 'Arab-sponsored' (JTA).

I found no count of General Assembly or Human Rights Council resolutions from the UN's own records or from a peer-reviewed study. Every count of Assembly resolutions traces to UN Watch (advocacy); the AP count of 233 Council resolutions is from 2016 and the AP does not say how it counted. The three non-advocacy sources on the Assembly count (Scripps, CBC, Hoover) mostly repeat or build on UN Watch's numbers, so they are not independent counts, and the card says so.
Ban Ki-moon's statement is quoted only as cited in the Hoover working paper; I did not read his remarks at the Security Council directly.
The sentence that the resolution passed 'in the middle of the Cold War' and 'most of the resolutions concern the occupation' rests on the sources above; I did not classify the resolutions myself.
The arguments that delegates gave for 3379 (for example that Zionism resembles South African apartheid) could not be read from a primary record; only the preamble is quoted.

Fact 6 (Assembly resolution counts) is short: every count traces to UN Watch's database, an advocacy group; the Scripps fact check and CBC repeat it, and the Hoover paper gives no total. I looked for a count from the UN's own records or a peer-reviewed study and found none, so it is UN Watch's count and the card says so.
The 1991 resolution's own text could not be read from a UN page; the UN's index of 46th-session resolutions (research.un.org) records the number, date and vote.

The Euronews page gives '124-12' in one paragraph and '124-14' in another; Daily Sabah and the Italian outlet give 124 in favour, and the 14 against comes from Euronews and Daily Sabah. I did not read the vote on a UN page.
The Moynihan words are quoted from the American Rhetoric transcript (the Congressional Record text could not be read); the Marginalia Review and the Algemeiner quote the same line.
not_claimed: This card does not say the United Nations is biased against Israel, and it does not say it is not.
It does not say Zionism is racism; the General Assembly itself revoked that determination in 1991.

It does not say all criticism of Israel at the UN is illegitimate. The Assembly's 2024 resolution rests on the ICJ's findings, and the occupation's costs to Palestinians are facts on this card and the West Bank card.
It does not rest on UN Watch's counts as neutral data; they are labelled advocacy and come with the fact-checkers' caveat.

answer_claims.says: On 10 November 1975 the UN General Assembly voted 72 to 35, with 32 abstentions, that Zionism is a form of racism.

The UN roll call lists the Soviet bloc, China, Arab and Muslim states, India, and also Brazil, Mexico, Portugal and Malta voting yes; the United States, Israel and most Western European states voted no.
Israel's ambassador Chaim Herzog and US ambassador Daniel Patrick Moynihan denounced it that day.
On 16 December 1991 the Assembly revoked it, 111 to 25, with 13 abstentions, as the Soviet bloc collapsed.

Today, by UN Watch's count, the Assembly passed 173 resolutions on Israel against 80 on all other countries together from 2015 to 2024, and the Human Rights Council keeps a standing agenda item on Israel; the UN keeps no official count, and a fact check says such counts do not by themselves prove bias.

skeptic.notes: Read the Bochum roll call (adds the full yes/no/abstain lists), the Herzog and Moynihan transcripts, JTA on the shredding and the 1991 repeal, Scripps, CBC, the UN Watch page, the Hoover working paper, Euronews, Daily Sabah, La Voce. The 72-35-32 and 111-25-13 votes, the Herzog and Moynihan words, and the preamble are on the pages. [must-fix] Fact 6 is short: Scripps (173 v 80), CBC (15 in a year) and UN Watch itself are one dataset, and Scripps says so ('according to UN Watch's database'); I added wire 'UN Watch' to all three, leaving only the Hoover paper (which gives no total) as independent. It needs a count from UN records or a peer-reviewed study. Fact 7's 233-resolution AP figure and UN Watch's 99 (2006-2022) are unreconciled and the AP piece does not say how it counted; the same page also lists Syria 41, Iran 13, Russia 4, which the fact leaves out. [must-fix, fixed] Fact 8 opened 'Many of the resolutions concern the occupation' with one resolution as support; reworded. The two Euronews entries are one AP-bylined story (wire added). [should-fix] Palestinian/non-Soviet counter-fact: the roll call shows yes votes from Brazil, Mexico, Cuba, India, Yugoslavia, Portugal, Malta and Cyprus, and abstentions from Greece and Japan; 'Cold War setting' and 'Soviet product' (Time, Center for Israel Education) explain the Soviet role but under-describe who voted yes. The Cambridge source's 'PLO victory' is on the card; the delegates' own arguments (comparison with South African apartheid beyond the preamble) are not. [should-fix] Israeli lawyer: the card has no source on why the Council has a standing Item 7 or on whether Israel's exclusion from a regional group explains the counts; the Scripps fact check is the only caveat. [nit] Fact 4: only the American Rhetoric transcript contains the quoted words. 'Time' is a 1991 magazine article cited for 1975.

citer.notes: Five answer sentences, each tied to facts. Removed: 'The UN is still lopsided on Israel' (a verdict the card's own not_claimed says it does not make); 'though the count is mostly UN Watch's' reworded to 'by UN Watch's count' with the fact-check caveat; and 'most of the resolutions concern the occupation', which no source supports (only one 2024 resolution is on the card). Reworded the Cold War sentence to what fact 2 and the roll call carry: 'many African and non-aligned states' became 'about half the African states and some Asian states', and 'Western Europe' became 'most Western European states' (Portugal and Malta voted yes, Greece abstained). I could not support the word 'non-aligned' in the vote.
